implementation: Seed transfer plus incremental release of worker DISTINCT state; existing floating SUM/AVG worker order retained.
COUNT/MIN/MAX-only shared DISTINCT lanes retain encoded keys/index without representative rows; SUM/AVG and standalone DISTINCT keep payload.
Allocator-backed reusable borrowed spill frames/offsets; owned scan batches; direct sort/lane merging; reusable minimal dedup/group keys.
Large valid records transfer frame ownership when the batching allowance is insufficient; old per-record wire admission retained.
Spill-backed budget/cancellation failures return correct structured execution codes.
limitations: Synthetic workloads, not official TPC/ClickBench results or universal engine rankings.
Native timing is normal pure-Go amd64; ARM64 has compile checks only.
Cumulative Go B/op is distinct from requested live allocator bytes and sampled process RSS; borrowed inputs, Go metadata and unused slab capacity are outside query scope.
Buffer reuse slightly raises live spill peaks. Large retained results and individual records/pages still must fit the query budget.
Disk spilling remains opt-in, nonadaptive, with unchanged eligibility/composition boundaries.
Four-engine smoke timings validate results and are not used for engine speed rankings.
The primary matrix includes a tiny four-worker wide-output regression (0.121 to 0.147 ms); an isolated 120-sample recheck measures 0.133 to 0.136 ms. Both results are retained.
386 cursor tests used an overlay for an unrelated existing typed-test compile failure; no whole-project 386 support claim.
